run.question: Which service has the most error events in the events collection? What is the most common error code for that service and how many times does it appear?

report.summary: In the MongoDB `events` collection of the configured database opsdb (the only collection present), payment-processor has the most error-level events: 47, ahead of inventory-sync (31), user-auth (25), notification-hub (18) and search-indexer (12). For payment-processor the most common error code is TXN-4821, which appears 23 times, with message "Transaction timeout waiting for bank response"; it is followed by TXN-5190 (14 occurrences, "Currency conversion service unavailable") and TXN-3007 (10 occurrences, "Duplicate transaction ID detected"). These counts come from direct MongoDB aggregations over the collection as it is at query time; the collection holds 133 level=error and 67 level=info documents (200 total). One important scope caveat: the timestamps of these documents are 2025-12-01T00:00:00 to 2025-12-01T02:12:00, i.e. a year before the authorized window (2026-10-24T18:51:16Z to 2026-11-23T18:51:16Z), so this answers what the collection contains, not what happened during the authorized window. No root cause is asserted: this was a data question about the events collection, and no fault attribution was investigated.

claims.text: The configured database opsdb contains exactly one collection, named `events`, with estimated_document_count 200 and fields _id, error_code, level, message, service, timestamp.
The `events` collection contains 133 documents with level="error" and 67 with level="info" (grouping by the level field).
Ranking services by error-level event count: payment-processor 47, inventory-sync 31, user-auth 25, notification-hub 18, search-indexer 12 — payment-processor is the highest.
For service payment-processor the error_code counts are TXN-4821 = 23, TXN-5190 = 14, TXN-3007 = 10, so TXN-4821 is the most common error code and it appears 23 times.

Grouping payment-processor documents by error_code and message shows the error texts verbatim: TXN-4821 "Transaction timeout waiting for bank response" (23), TXN-5190 "Currency conversion service unavailable" (14), TXN-3007 "Duplicate transaction ID detected" (10); the remaining payment-processor documents are level=info messages without an error_code (e.g. "Health check passed", "Request processed successfully", 2 each).

A sample of payment-processor error documents shows consecutive minute-spaced records, e.g. error_code TXN-4821 with message "Transaction timeout waiting for bank response" at 2025-12-01T00:00:00, 00:01:00, 00:02:00, 00:03:00 and 00:04:00.

The error-level documents' timestamps span 2025-12-01T00:00:00 to 2025-12-01T02:12:00, which lies outside the authorized window 2026-10-24T18:51:16Z – 2026-11-23T18:51:16Z (Python-MongoDB reads here are not filtered by that window).

The ranking is not an artifact of filtering on level: grouping all 200 documents by service regardless of level gives the same order — payment-processor 61, inventory-sync 45, user-auth 38, notification-hub 31, search-indexer 25 — so payment-processor is also the service with the most events overall.

The service labels used in the `events` collection (payment-processor, inventory-sync, user-auth, notification-hub, search-indexer) do not match any of the trace service names available in this environment (accounting, ad, cart, checkout, currency, email, fraud-detection, frontend, frontend-proxy, image-provider, kafka, load-generator, payment, product-catalog, quote, recommendation, shipping); whether "payment-processor" corresponds to the traced "payment" service cannot be established from this evidence and would require a verified mapping.

gaps: The events documents are all timestamped 2025-12-01, about 12 months before the authorized window; no events-collection content inside the authorized window (2026-10-24T18:51:16Z – 2026-11-23T18:51:16Z) was observed, so nothing can be said about error events during that window.

No mapping was observable between the events-collection service names (e.g. payment-processor) and the Jaeger/Prometheus service names (e.g. payment, checkout), so it is unknown which monitored workload payment-processor corresponds to.
The change_history integration is not configured in this Run, so whether the payment-processor timeout pattern coincides with a deployment or configuration change could not be checked.
MongoDB reads show the database as it is at query time only; whether documents were added, removed or altered during the authorized window is unknown.
next_steps: Confirm with the collection's owner whether the 2025-12-01 timestamped events are historical seed/backfill data or a clock/timezone artifact, since they fall outside the incident window.

If these errors are meant to be correlated with live telemetry, obtain the mapping between the events collection service labels (payment-processor, inventory-sync, user-auth, notification-hub, search-indexer) and the Jaeger service names.

Investigate the TXN-4821 "Transaction timeout waiting for bank response" path (23 of 47 payment-processor errors) in payment's dependency on an external bank/currency dependency via traces for the service the mapping identifies.
